about.quote: We use technology to simplify, not complicate. Every project should solve a business problem — looking good is a bonus.

caseStudy.title: Gel Gez Gor — North Cyprus {accent} classifieds platform.
caseStudy.body1: We designed and developed Gel Gez Gor from scratch — a comprehensive free classifieds platform for North Cyprus. The platform hosts thousands of listings across real estate, vehicles, jobs, and food categories.
caseStudy.body2: With advanced filtering, user-friendly interface, and SEO optimization, we helped it become one of the most visited classifieds sites in North Cyprus.

chrome.availability: Open for new projects · Let's start

velis-ltd.title: Velis LTD
velis-ltd.summary: Construction company corporate site with product catalog.
body: We designed a corporate website for Velis LTD that reflects over 25 years of industry experience. Built on WordPress with a product catalog, multi-language support, and SEO optimization.
We created a professional digital identity for the construction and manufacturing sector. Responsive design, fast load times, and easy content management strengthened the client's digital presence.

bt-elevator.title: BT Elevator
bt-elevator.summary: Multi-language elevator company website with SEO optimization.
body: We designed and developed the corporate website for BT Elevator, an elevator company based in Eskisehir, Turkey. Multi-language structure, SEO optimization, and modern design created a standout digital presence in the industry.
Technical SEO work, schema markup, and performance optimization targeted top search engine rankings. We delivered a trust-building user experience aligned with the corporate identity.

gel-gez-gor.title: Gel Gez Gor
gel-gez-gor.summary: Free classifieds platform for North Cyprus with multiple categories.
body: We designed and developed Gel Gez Gor, a comprehensive free classifieds platform for North Cyprus. We built a dynamic platform hosting thousands of listings across real estate, vehicles, jobs, and food categories.
With a user-friendly interface, advanced filtering system, and SEO optimization, we helped it become one of the most visited classifieds sites in North Cyprus.

nexon-investment.title: Nexon Investment
nexon-investment.summary: Real estate and investment company website in North Cyprus.
body: We developed a corporate website focused on real estate and investment for Nexon Investment, based in Famagusta, North Cyprus. We created a professional digital presence that informs and builds trust with investors.
Modern design, fast load times, and mobile-responsive structure made it easy for potential investors to access information. SEO efforts increased organic visibility.

ambalaj-cini.title: Ambalaj Cini
ambalaj-cini.summary: E-commerce packaging supplies store with payment integration.
body: We developed an online packaging supplies sales platform for Ambalaj Cini, based in Bilecik, Turkey. We built a comprehensive e-commerce infrastructure including payment integration, product management, and inventory tracking.
User experience-focused design, easy ordering flow, and secure payment infrastructure significantly increased the client's online sales. Actively serving since 2022.

avie-global.title: Avie Global
avie-global.summary: Automotive spare parts trading company corporate website.
body: We designed a corporate website for Avie Global Trading in the automotive spare parts trading sector. Built on WordPress, we created a professional platform showcasing the company profile, product range, and business partnerships.
Global trade-focused design, multi-language content structure, and SEO optimization targeted reaching international customers.

web-design.title: Web Design
web-design.desc: Brand-driven marketing sites with considered type, motion, and editorial rhythm.
web-design.longDesc: We design marketing sites that move with intention — every typographic choice, spacing decision, and motion detail serves the brand story. The result is a site that feels authored, not assembled. We work from strategy to final pixel, covering information architecture, interaction design, and handoff-ready component systems.

features.title: Brand-First Layout
features.desc: Every layout starts from the brand's visual language, not a template. Grid, type scale, and spacing are derived from the identity.

features.title: Editorial Typography
features.desc: Type is treated as the primary design element — scale, rhythm, and hierarchy are set before color or imagery.

features.title: Motion Design
features.desc: Purposeful animation that enhances storytelling without distracting. Entrances, transitions, and micro-interactions are storyboarded.

features.title: Design Systems
features.desc: Component libraries with documented tokens, variants, and usage guidelines — so your team can extend the design without breaking it.

features.title: Responsive First
features.desc: Every breakpoint is designed, not just resized. Mobile is a first-class experience, not an afterthought.

features.title: CMS Integration
features.desc: Contentful, Sanity, or headless setups that let non-technical editors publish at pace without touching code.

process.title: Discovery
process.desc: Brand audit, competitor analysis, stakeholder interviews. We establish what the site needs to say and who it needs to say it to.

process.title: Architecture
process.desc: Sitemap, content model, and page wireframes. Structure before style.

process.title: Visual Direction
process.desc: Two visual directions explored, one developed. Type, color, and layout language defined.

process.title: Design Build
process.desc: Full-fidelity Figma components across all breakpoints, with interaction specs and motion notes.

process.title: Handoff
process.desc: Developer-ready files, design tokens exported, component annotations, and a recorded walkthrough.

faq.q: Do you build the site or just design it?
faq.a: Both. We offer design-only engagements for teams with developers, and full design-to-code delivery. Most clients take the full package.

faq.q: What if we already have a brand?
faq.a: We work with existing brand systems and extend them into digital. We'll audit what you have and adapt rather than override.

faq.q: How many revision rounds are included?
faq.a: Two rounds per major phase. Additional rounds are billed at our hourly rate. In practice, we rarely hit that limit because we align early.

faq.q: Can you work with our existing CMS?
faq.a: Yes — we've built on Webflow, Framer, WordPress, Contentful, Sanity, and custom Next.js setups. We'll recommend what fits your team's workflow.

web-app.title: Web App
web-app.desc: Full-stack product surfaces — dashboards, tools, internal systems that hold up at scale.
web-app.longDesc: We build product-grade web applications that handle real load, real users, and real complexity. From the data model to the dashboard UI, every layer is considered. We specialize in Next.js full-stack builds with authentication, billing, role-based access, and real-time features — shipped with observability from day one.

features.title: Full-Stack Architecture
features.desc: Next.js App Router with server components, API routes, and edge functions. TypeScript throughout, no compromises.

features.title: Auth & Roles
features.desc: Multi-tenant auth with role-based access control. SSO, social login, magic links — whatever your user base needs.

features.title: Billing Integration
features.desc: Stripe subscriptions, usage-based billing, metered features, and customer portal — wired in from the start, not bolted on later.

features.title: Realtime Features
features.desc: WebSockets, server-sent events, and optimistic UI for collaborative or live-updating interfaces.

features.title: API Design
features.desc: RESTful or tRPC APIs with typed contracts, rate limiting, and versioning strategy built in.

features.title: Observability
features.desc: Error tracking, performance monitoring, and structured logging from day one. You'll know what's breaking before users do.

process.title: Scoping
process.desc: Requirements workshop, technical spec, and architecture decision records. Nothing ambiguous going into build.

process.title: Data Model
process.desc: Schema design, relationships, and indexing strategy before a line of application code is written.

process.title: Core Build
process.desc: Auth, routing, and data layer first. UI components follow once the foundation is solid.

process.title: Feature Sprints
process.desc: Two-week sprints with deployed previews after every sprint. Feedback integrated before moving forward.

process.title: Launch
process.desc: Production environment setup, monitoring configured, documentation written, and team handover session.

faq.q: Do you work with an existing codebase?
faq.a: Yes. We've joined projects mid-way, refactored legacy codebases, and extended existing products. We always start with an audit.

faq.q: What database do you use?
faq.a: Postgres for most projects, with Prisma or Drizzle as the ORM. We'll use what's already in your stack if you have one.

faq.q: Do you handle DevOps?
faq.a: We set up the infrastructure as part of the build — CI/CD, preview environments, and production on Vercel or Google Cloud. Long-term DevOps is a separate engagement.

faq.q: How do you handle security?
faq.a: OWASP top-10 is baseline. We also do input validation, CSRF protection, rate limiting, and dependency audits as part of standard delivery.

progressive-web-app.title: Progressive Web App
progressive-web-app.desc: App-like experiences that run in the browser — installable, offline-capable, and no app store required.
progressive-web-app.longDesc: We build Progressive Web Apps that blur the line between website and native app. Installable on any device, working offline, sending push notifications — all without the friction of app store submission. PWAs load instantly, work on any platform, and cost a fraction of native development while delivering 90% of the same experience.

features.title: Installable
features.desc: Add to Home Screen with a native-looking app icon. Your users launch it like a real app — no browser chrome, full-screen experience.

features.title: Offline First
features.desc: Service Workers cache critical assets and data. Your app works without a connection and syncs cleanly when it reconnects.

features.title: Push Notifications
features.desc: Web Push API for re-engagement — segmented, scheduled, and deep-linked, just like native push.

features.title: Instant Loading
features.desc: Pre-cached shell architecture with streaming SSR. First paint under 1 second, even on slow connections.

features.title: Cross-Platform
features.desc: One codebase runs everywhere — iOS Safari, Android Chrome, desktop — with platform-appropriate behavior on each.

features.title: Auto Updates
features.desc: No app store review cycles. Deploy and your users get the latest version on next visit — silently, instantly.

process.title: Audit & Strategy
process.desc: Evaluate which native features you actually need vs. what the web platform already provides. Most teams are surprised.

process.title: App Shell Design
process.desc: Design the installable shell — splash screen, navigation, offline UI states. Feels native from first launch.

process.title: Core Build
process.desc: Next.js + Service Worker setup. Caching strategies, background sync, and push notification infrastructure.

process.title: Testing
process.desc: Lighthouse audit (100/100 PWA score target), cross-browser testing, offline scenario validation on real devices.

process.title: Launch
process.desc: Web App Manifest configured, HTTPS enforced, analytics tracking installed. Your PWA is live everywhere instantly.

faq.q: PWA vs native app — when to choose which?
faq.a: PWA covers 90% of use cases — content apps, dashboards, e-commerce, tools. Go native only if you need hardware APIs like Bluetooth, NFC, or advanced camera controls.

faq.q: Do PWAs work on iPhone?
faq.a: Yes. iOS Safari supports installable PWAs, Service Workers, and offline caching. Push notifications arrived in iOS 16.4. The gap with Android is now minimal.

faq.q: Can users install it from the browser?
faq.a: Yes — both Chrome and Safari prompt users to 'Add to Home Screen'. The app appears alongside native apps with its own icon.

faq.q: What about SEO?
faq.a: PWAs are just websites — fully indexable by Google. You get the SEO benefits of a website plus the engagement of an app.

automation.title: Automation
automation.desc: Workflow pipelines that quietly replace the spreadsheets no one wants to open.
automation.longDesc: We map your manual processes and replace them with reliable, observable automation pipelines. Whether it's n8n self-hosted on your infrastructure, Zapier for low-code simplicity, or custom-built webhook handlers — we match the tool to the job. The goal is to eliminate the work that shouldn't require a human.

features.title: Process Mapping
features.desc: We document the current manual workflow before touching any tooling. Understanding the process is 80% of the job.

features.title: n8n Self-Hosted
features.desc: Full control over your automations with n8n on your own infrastructure. No per-execution pricing, no vendor lock-in.

features.title: Zapier & Make
features.desc: Rapid deployment for teams that need automation without infrastructure overhead. Right tool for the right job.

features.title: Internal Tools
features.desc: Custom admin panels, approval workflows, and data management UIs built on top of your automation layer.

features.title: Webhook Architecture
features.desc: Event-driven pipelines with retry logic, dead letter queues, and idempotency handling.

features.title: Scheduled Jobs
features.desc: Cron-based data sync, report generation, and maintenance tasks with monitoring and alerting.

process.title: Process Audit
process.desc: Interview the people doing the manual work. Map every step, decision point, and exception case.

process.title: Automation Design
process.desc: Design the automated workflow with error handling and edge cases documented before implementation.

process.title: Build & Test
process.desc: Implement with staging environment testing. Every automation is tested against real data before production.

process.title: Monitoring Setup
process.desc: Alerts for failures, execution logs, and dashboards so you know when something breaks.

process.title: Handover
process.desc: Documentation, training for your team, and a 30-day support window post-launch.

faq.q: We already use Zapier — can you improve what we have?
faq.a: Absolutely. We audit existing Zaps, identify fragile steps, and rebuild or extend them. Often we migrate the most complex ones to n8n.

faq.q: What if the process changes after you build it?
faq.a: We document everything so your team can maintain it. For ongoing changes, we offer retainer support.

faq.q: Can you automate across multiple tools?
faq.a: Yes — multi-system automations are our specialty. CRM, ERP, Slack, email, databases, and custom APIs all connected.

faq.q: Is n8n hard to manage?
faq.a: We handle the infrastructure setup and make it manageable. Most clients find it easier than expected after the initial setup.

ai-integration.title: AI Integration
ai-integration.desc: LLMs, RAG, and agents wired into real products — evaluated, guard-railed, observable.
ai-integration.longDesc: We integrate large language models into real products responsibly — with evaluation frameworks, guardrails, cost controls, and observability built in. We work with Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini, and we choose models based on your use case, not familiarity. RAG pipelines, agent architectures, and tool-use systems are our specialty.

features.title: Model Selection
features.desc: We evaluate models against your specific use case — latency, cost, quality, and capability all factored in. No defaults.

features.title: RAG Pipelines
features.desc: Retrieval-augmented generation with vector databases, chunking strategies, and re-ranking. Your data, accurately surfaced.

features.title: Agent Architecture
features.desc: Multi-step agents with tool-use, memory, and planning. Built to complete complex tasks reliably, not just impressively.

features.title: Evaluation Framework
features.desc: Custom eval suites that measure what matters for your use case. No vibes-based quality assessment.

features.title: Guardrails
features.desc: Input/output filtering, content policies, and safety layers that match your risk tolerance and regulatory environment.

features.title: Observability
features.desc: Trace every LLM call, track costs, monitor latency, and alert on quality regressions. LLMOps from the start.

process.title: Use Case Scoping
process.desc: Define the problem the AI should solve and the metrics that define success. Avoid building before you know what 'good' looks like.

process.title: Prototype & Eval
process.desc: Rapid prototype tested against real data. Evaluation suite built alongside the prototype, not after.

process.title: Pipeline Build
process.desc: Production-grade implementation with error handling, fallbacks, and cost controls.

process.title: Guardrails & Safety
process.desc: Input validation, output filtering, and adversarial testing before any user-facing deployment.

process.title: Monitor & Iterate
process.desc: Post-launch monitoring with regular quality reviews and model updates as the landscape evolves.

faq.q: Which LLM should we use?
faq.a: It depends on your use case. We'll run a structured evaluation against your actual data and recommend based on results, not hype.

faq.q: How do you handle hallucinations?
faq.a: RAG grounds responses in your data. Eval suites catch regressions. Guardrails catch harmful outputs. No single solution — defense in depth.

faq.q: What does an AI integration cost to run?
faq.a: We model inference costs as part of the design. Most integrations we build cost $0.01–$0.10 per user session at scale.

faq.q: Can you improve an existing AI feature?
faq.a: Yes. We audit the current implementation, identify the failure modes, and improve the pipeline systematically.

google-ads.title: Google Ads
google-ads.desc: Search, performance-max, and display campaigns built around conversion paths, not vanity metrics.
google-ads.longDesc: We run Google Ads campaigns that are built around your actual conversion path — not impressions, not clicks, not awareness. Every campaign structure, bidding strategy, and creative decision is tied to a measurable business outcome. We set up conversion tracking properly before spending a dollar on ads.

features.title: Campaign Architecture
features.desc: Account structure designed for performance — the right match types, negative keywords, and ad group segmentation from day one.

features.title: Search Campaigns
features.desc: Intent-based search campaigns targeting buyers, not browsers. Copy written to match the search context, not to impress.

features.title: Performance Max
features.desc: PMax campaigns built with strong asset groups and audience signals — not left to Google's defaults.

features.title: Conversion Tracking
features.desc: GA4, Google Ads, and server-side tracking set up accurately. You can't optimize what you can't measure.

features.title: Creative Testing
features.desc: Systematic ad copy and creative testing with statistical significance thresholds. No gut-feel decisions.

features.title: Reporting
features.desc: Weekly reports focused on business metrics — leads, revenue, ROAS — not vanity metrics.

process.title: Audit & Setup
process.desc: Existing account audit (or new account setup), conversion tracking verification, and baseline measurement.

process.title: Campaign Build
process.desc: Campaign structure, keyword research, ad copy, and landing page alignment.

process.title: Launch & Learn
process.desc: Two-week learning period with daily monitoring. No major changes until the algorithm has sufficient data.

process.title: Optimize
process.desc: Weekly optimization cycles: bid adjustments, negative keywords, creative testing, audience refinement.

process.title: Scale
process.desc: Proven campaigns scaled methodically. Budget increases tied to efficiency thresholds, not ambition.

faq.q: What budget do we need to start?
faq.a: Minimum $1,500/month ad spend. Below that, the learning period takes too long to generate meaningful data.

faq.q: How long until we see results?
faq.a: The first 4 weeks are the learning period. Meaningful optimization starts in week 5–6. Month 3 is typically when efficiency peaks.

faq.q: Do you work with existing campaigns?
faq.a: Yes. We audit first, identify the biggest losses, and fix those before building new campaigns.

faq.q: Is the management fee separate from ad spend?
faq.a: Yes. You pay Google directly for ad spend. Our management fee is separate and covers strategy, setup, and optimization.

seo-geo.title: SEO & GEO
seo-geo.desc: Technical SEO plus generative-engine optimization — being found by Google and by models.
seo-geo.longDesc: SEO in 2025 means being found by both search engines and language models. We handle technical SEO — Core Web Vitals, schema markup, crawlability — and generative engine optimization: structuring your content so it's cited by Claude, ChatGPT, and Perplexity. These are different problems with different solutions, and we address both.

features.title: Technical SEO Audit
features.desc: Crawl analysis, Core Web Vitals, indexation issues, duplicate content, and redirect chains. Everything that affects how Google sees your site.

features.title: Schema Markup
features.desc: Structured data that tells search engines exactly what your content is — Organization, Product, Article, FAQ, and custom schemas.

features.title: Core Web Vitals
features.desc: LCP, INP, and CLS optimization at the code level. We work with your dev team to implement, not just report.

features.title: Content Strategy
features.desc: Topic cluster mapping, content gap analysis, and editorial calendar built around search intent, not just volume.

features.title: GEO (Generative Engine)
features.desc: Structuring content so language models can accurately cite and summarize it. A different discipline from traditional SEO.

features.title: LLM Citation Surfaces
features.desc: Building the authoritative content, structured data, and link profile that makes models choose you as a source.

process.title: Technical Audit
process.desc: Full crawl, Core Web Vitals measurement, and indexation analysis. Prioritized fix list with effort/impact estimates.

process.title: Fix Implementation
process.desc: Technical fixes implemented alongside your dev team. We write the specs; we can implement too if needed.

process.title: Content Map
process.desc: Topic clusters, content gaps, and a 6-month editorial calendar tied to search intent and business goals.

process.title: GEO Layer
process.desc: Schema markup, structured content formats, and authority-building content specifically for LLM citation.

process.title: Monitor & Iterate
process.desc: Monthly reporting on rankings, traffic, and citation mentions. Strategy adjusted as the landscape evolves.

faq.q: What's GEO and why does it matter?
faq.a: Generative Engine Optimization is the practice of making your content citable by AI models. As more users get answers from AI, being cited by Claude or ChatGPT becomes as important as ranking on Google.

faq.q: How long does SEO take?
faq.a: Technical fixes show results in 2–4 weeks. Content impact takes 3–6 months. GEO results are harder to measure but typically visible in 2–3 months.

faq.q: Do you write the content?
faq.a: We can write, brief, or review. Most clients have their own writers and use us for strategy and optimization.

faq.q: Can you work with our existing CMS?
faq.a: Yes. We've optimized content on WordPress, Contentful, Sanity, Webflow, and custom setups. Schema and meta implementation adapts to your stack.

how-to-do.title: How To Do?
how-to-do.desc: Hands-on training, workshops, and mentorship — we make your team self-sufficient.
how-to-do.longDesc: We deliver hands-on training in software, design, and digital marketing. Not theoretical but practice-focused: real projects, real tools, curriculum customized to your team's needs. Our goal isn't to create dependency — it's to make your team independent and capable.

features.title: Hands-On Workshops
features.desc: Half-day or full-day team workshops. We work on real projects with live coding and design.

features.title: 1:1 Mentorship
features.desc: Personalized mentorship for individual development. We work on your project, with your actual challenges.

features.title: Video Training Series
features.desc: Step-by-step video courses — Next.js, React, Supabase, AI integration, SEO, and more.

features.title: Developing with AI
features.desc: How to develop 5x faster with Claude Code, Cursor, and AI tools — from first repo to production.

features.title: Team Playbooks
features.desc: Internal documentation written specifically for your team's technologies, workflow rules, and best practice guides.

features.title: Ongoing Advisory
features.desc: Monthly check-ins to track team progress, resolve bottlenecks, and teach new patterns.

process.title: Needs Analysis
process.desc: The team's current skill level, tools used, and goals are assessed. The training curriculum is designed accordingly.

process.title: Curriculum Design
process.desc: Exercises and workshop content tailored to your actual project and tech stack are prepared.

process.title: Training Delivery
process.desc: Live, hands-on session. Everyone delivers something real by the end of the session.

process.title: Documentation
process.desc: Post-training patterns, conventions, and reference cards specific to your team are written.

process.title: Follow-Up & Mentorship
process.desc: Optional 1:1 mentorship sessions for those who want to dive deeper after training.

faq.q: What topics do you offer training on?
faq.a: Web development (Next.js, React), AI tools (Claude Code, Cursor), databases (Supabase, PostgreSQL), SEO, automation, and digital marketing. We customize based on your needs.

faq.q: Do you offer online training?
faq.a: Yes. Online workshops work great for up to 12 people. For larger groups, we recommend in-person training.

faq.q: Is there a minimum skill level required?
faq.a: Depends on the topic. Basic programming knowledge is enough for technical training. Marketing training is open to everyone.

faq.q: How do we measure ROI?
faq.a: We measure sprint velocity, delivery quality, and team satisfaction before and after training. Most teams report a 3-5x productivity increase.

data-engineering.title: Data Engineering
data-engineering.desc: Warehouses, ELT pipelines, and analytics layers your team can actually query.
data-engineering.longDesc: We build data infrastructure that your team actually uses — clean schemas, reliable pipelines, and dashboards that answer real questions. From raw event streams to executive dashboards, we handle the full analytics stack. The goal is a data warehouse your team trusts enough to make decisions from.

features.title: Warehouse Design
features.desc: Dimensional modeling in BigQuery, Snowflake, or Postgres. Schemas designed for both query performance and team usability.

features.title: ELT Pipelines
features.desc: Airbyte for extraction, dbt for transformation. Every transformation tested, documented, and version-controlled.

features.title: dbt Models
features.desc: Modular dbt project with staging, intermediate, and mart layers. Every model has tests and documentation.

features.title: Orchestration
features.desc: Airflow or Prefect for pipeline scheduling, monitoring, and failure handling. No silent failures.

features.title: Metrics Layer
features.desc: Semantic layer with consistent metric definitions across all dashboards. One source of truth for 'revenue' and 'active users'.

features.title: Dashboards
features.desc: Looker, Metabase, or Superset dashboards built around actual business questions, not what the tool makes easy.

process.title: Data Audit
process.desc: Inventory of existing data sources, quality assessment, and identification of the 5 questions the business most needs to answer.

process.title: Architecture Design
process.desc: Warehouse selection, schema design, and pipeline architecture documented before any code.

process.title: Pipeline Build
process.desc: ELT pipelines with data quality checks, alerting, and incremental loading from the start.

process.title: Transform Layer
process.desc: dbt models covering all core business entities with tests and documentation.

process.title: Dashboard Delivery
process.desc: Business dashboards built with stakeholders, not for them. Iteration included.

faq.q: Which warehouse should we use?
faq.a: BigQuery for GCP shops, Snowflake for enterprise, Postgres for early-stage. We'll recommend based on your team size, budget, and existing stack.

faq.q: We have messy, inconsistent data — can you still help?
faq.a: That's the typical starting point. Data cleaning and normalization is part of the dbt transformation layer.

faq.q: Do you train our team on dbt?
faq.a: Yes. Knowledge transfer is part of every engagement. We don't build black boxes.

faq.q: How do you handle PII and data privacy?
faq.a: Column-level masking, role-based access, and data classification as standard. We can also help with GDPR/CCPA compliance requirements.

cloud-ecosystem.title: Cloud Ecosystem
cloud-ecosystem.desc: Production-grade cloud setups across Google Cloud and Vercel — observable, documented, handover-ready.
cloud-ecosystem.longDesc: We design and build cloud infrastructure that's production-ready from day one — not just something that works, but something observable, documented, and safe to hand over. Google Cloud for backend infrastructure, Vercel for frontend deployment, Terraform for infrastructure-as-code, and a monitoring stack that tells you what's happening before users notice it isn't.

features.title: Infrastructure as Code
features.desc: Terraform modules for all infrastructure. Everything reproducible, version-controlled, and reviewable.

features.title: Google Cloud Architecture
features.desc: Cloud Run, GKE, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage, Cloud CDN — Google's managed services right-sized for your workload.

features.title: Vercel Deployment
features.desc: Edge-optimized frontend hosting with preview deployments, ISR, and serverless functions — the fastest path from commit to production.

features.title: CI/CD Pipelines
features.desc: GitHub Actions workflows with automated testing, preview deployments, and controlled production releases.

features.title: Monitoring Stack
features.desc: Google Cloud Monitoring, Grafana, or Datadog configured to alert on what matters. Dashboards your on-call team will actually use.

features.title: Documentation
features.desc: Architecture decision records, runbooks, and incident response playbooks. Your team can operate it after we leave.

process.title: Architecture Review
process.desc: Current state assessment, bottleneck identification, and future-state architecture design with tradeoffs documented.

process.title: IaC Migration
process.desc: Existing infrastructure codified in Terraform. No more click-ops.

process.title: CI/CD Build
process.desc: Automated pipelines for all environments — dev, staging, production — with deployment gates and rollback procedures.

process.title: Monitoring Setup
process.desc: Alerts, dashboards, and on-call runbooks configured and tested before go-live.

process.title: Handover
process.desc: Documentation package, team training session, and 30-day support window.

faq.q: Why Google Cloud over AWS?
faq.a: Google Cloud offers superior managed services, better pricing models, and tighter integration with AI/ML tooling. For most workloads we handle, GCP + Vercel is the optimal combination.

faq.q: Do you manage the infrastructure ongoing?
faq.a: We set up and hand over. Ongoing management retainers are available but most clients prefer to own their infrastructure after we've set it up well.

faq.q: How do you handle disaster recovery?
faq.a: RTO and RPO targets defined in the architecture phase, with tested recovery procedures. DR isn't an afterthought.

faq.q: Do you work with Kubernetes?
faq.a: Yes. GKE on Google Cloud or self-managed. We'll recommend it when the complexity is justified — which is less often than people think.

dolmus.title: Dolmus
body: We developed the Dolmus web application, a minibus route tracking system for public transportation. Users can easily view routes and plan their travel.
Real-time route information, user-friendly interface, and mobile-responsive design made city transportation easier.

orchid-tent.title: Orchid Tent
orchid-tent.sub: London-based tent and event rental company.
body: We designed a corporate website for Orchid Tent, a London-based tent and event rental service. Elegant design and easy navigation allowed potential clients to quickly find information.
Event gallery, quote request form, and responsive design created a strong digital presence in London's event industry.

gabfest-2025.title: Gabfest 2025
body: We designed a modern and informative event website for the Gabfest 2025 conference on WordPress. We presented the program, speakers, and registration information in an organized manner.
We built a dynamic structure providing up-to-date information before, during, and after the event. Mobile-responsive design ensured easy access from any device.

kibris-night-club.title: Kibris Night Club
body: We developed an SEO-focused directory site listing nightclubs and entertainment venues in North Cyprus. Built on WordPress with venue profiles, event calendars, and user reviews.
SEO optimization achieved top search engine rankings for nightlife searches. User experience and fast access were our priorities.

aydin-transfer.title: Aydin Transfer
body: We designed a corporate website for Aydin Transfer offering airport and city transfer services. Easy booking flow, price calculator, and contact forms optimized the customer experience.
Mobile-responsive design and fast load times ensured passengers could easily book transfers anytime.
